explainer_content.short_definition: A California-coded early guitar-pop lane split between reverb-soaked instrumentals and harmony-rich beach-radio songs.
explainer_content.history_capsule: Surf music turns place into sound: ocean motion, hot rods, Southern California youth imagery, and electric-guitar technology. Dick Dale and The Chantays show the instrumental attack; The Beach Boys and Jan and Dean show how surf culture became vocal pop mythology.
explainer_content.why_it_mattered: It made guitar tone an environment. Its reverb, tremolo, fast picking, and wordless hooks echo through garage rock, film music, punk revival, and guitar instrumental culture.
explainer_content.what_made_it_distinct: The record often feels horizontal and kinetic, like motion across a surface: rolling drums, wet guitar, bright harmonies, and a scene you can picture immediately.
what_to_listen_for: Spring reverb around the lead guitar
Toms and snare patterns that mimic waves or motion
Surf, car, beach, and summer imagery
